content: An expansion joint was included in my upgrade kit.

a couple of steps later, people have been saying they split this part while running the screw in for the expansion joint.  I was able to do it without splitting the part (thanks to their warnings) and noted that the expansion joint has threads on the hole side that can cause the Allen key to hit and bind once you are near the end.  the M3x6r screw is torx so that contributes to the issue.  Here is what you do, find a thin, flat-blade screwdriver (jewelry screwdriver) that is wide enough to engage the M3x6r slots but thinner than the expansion joint hole that you have to go through.  start with the allen key, then switch to thin flat blade screwdriver.  Go slowly and do not try to work the screw tight because it will split due to the layer lines from printing orientation.  It can work, be slow, deliberate, and careful!!!!

If you're doing the INDX upgrade, then this whole step 21 is skipped, I assume?  The INDX has a completely different system for nozzle wiping.  Also, the parts mentionned here were not present in my Gen 2 upgrade kit delivered with the INDX.

replies.content: Yes, the "Assembling the Prusa INDX Core one with the Gen 2 upgrade" guide says to stop after the previous step ("Fixing the heatbed") is completed.

content: I received a bag of M3nN nuts with my kit, so I assume those are the ones needed for the following steps, not the M3n nut.

replies.content: Per the photo it appears to be M3nN nut, the n is for nylon I think, and the picture shows nylon on the inside of the nut.
